intro.title: Christmas baking without eggs using aquafaba
intro.description: Find out where aquafaba works in Christmas baking, how much to measure and when to whip it for cookies, cakes, sweet rolls and meringues.
intro.h1: How do I use a vegan egg replacer for Christmas baking?
intro.texto:
Use {egg_white_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for one egg white, or start with {whole_egg_g}g per whole egg in recipes where aquafaba can do the same job. Whip it for meringues and recipes that call for whipped whites. For a cookie dough that needs the egg to bind the ingredients, add the liquid without whipping.

If you’re baking a few things for Christmas, start with the recipe you know well. Once you’ve tried the swap in a small batch, you can plan the rest of the baking around it.

secciones.h2: What does the egg do in your bake?
secciones.texto:
Look at when the egg goes into the bowl. If it’s stirred into dough with the other liquids, it may be there to help hold the ingredients together or add moisture. If the recipe asks you to whip the whites before folding them in, the foam is part of what gives the bake its shape or lift.
What you’re bakingWhere to start
Christmas cookiesAdd aquafaba unwhipped where the egg is used for binding. Bake a small test tray.
Meringue cookiesWhip chilled aquafaba and follow the recipe’s sugar and drying steps.
Holiday sponge cakeCheck whether the recipe depends on whole-egg foam. Test the swap before making a layer cake.
Brioche or sweet rollsMeasure the aquafaba with the liquids and check the dough in a small bake.

secciones.h2: How much do you need?
secciones.texto:
Check the {egg_white_g}g or {whole_egg_g}g amount against the type of egg each recipe calls for, then weigh the liquid on your kitchen scale. For a recipe that uses whipped whites, keep any separate yolks in mind when you’re checking whether the finished bake will be egg-free.

If you’re using powder for egg whites, mix {powder_white_g}g with {powder_white_water} ml of water per white before adding it to the recipe. Use the recipe’s method to decide when the prepared aquafaba goes in.

secciones.h2: Try one bake before you fill the tins
secciones.texto: Keep the rest of the ingredients and the oven setting the same for your first test. For a suitable whole-egg swap in a recipe with added water or milk, start by reducing that liquid by {liquid_cut}%. Check that the cookies hold together when cool or that your sponge has the crumb you want before doubling anything. Once you’ve picked your bakes, work out how much aquafaba you need for the holidays from your recipe list.

secciones.h2: What can you keep the same on the first try?
secciones.texto:
Keep the tin, oven setting and main ingredients from the recipe you know. Make a note of how the egg normally goes in and what the mixture looks like at that point. If you’re testing a liquid swap, weigh it separately so you know how much went in. If a recipe calls for a foam, use a dedicated aquafaba method and follow its peak cues before moving on.

For a biscuit tray, give the test pieces time to cool before judging how they hold together. For a sponge, let the layer cool before you cut it or add a filling. Write down what you’d repeat. This is especially helpful if you’re baking the same thing on two different days.

secciones.h2: Check the rest of your gift or dessert
secciones.texto: A cookie dough can be egg-free while its decorations still contain egg. Check bought icing, glazes and other toppings as you make the shopping list. If you’re baking vegan too, check the fillings and chocolate for dairy. Keep the ingredient information with the biscuits or macarons if you’re giving them away.

faq.question: Can I use aquafaba in my Christmas cookie dough?
faq.answer: Try it where a whole egg binds the dough. Start with {whole_egg_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA and bake a few cookies to check the spread and texture.

faq.question: Do I need to whip aquafaba for Christmas baking?
faq.answer: Whip it for meringues or where your recipe calls for a foam. Add it as a liquid where the egg’s role is to bind the dough.

faq.question: How much aquafaba replaces one egg white?
faq.answer: Use {egg_white_g}g of liquid, or prepare {powder_white_g}g of powder with {powder_white_water} ml of water.

faq.question: Are bakes made with aquafaba always vegan?
faq.answer: Check the rest of the recipe. Butter, milk and decorations can introduce animal-derived ingredients even when you have replaced the egg.

faq.question: What can I make if I want to try a recipe designed for aquafaba?
faq.answer: Start with small meringues or a pavlova. Both have a measured aquafaba recipe with cues for whipping and baking.

Store the small meringues airtight once they’ve cooled.

Pick a dessert for the table and one for the cookie tin, or make a few of each. A pavlova works well as the centrepiece, and little mousse cups are easy to set out when people are ready for dessert.

faq.question: Can I assemble the pavlova the day before?
faq.answer: Bake and cool the base a day ahead. Keep it airtight and leave the cream and fruit until serving so the shell stays crisp.

faq.question: How long can I keep the mousse in the fridge?

faq.question: Which dessert takes the least work at the table?

intro.title: Egg-free holiday party sours to make at home
intro.description: Plan egg-free sours for your holiday party. Use {dose} ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink, mix the base ahead and shake fresh foam as you serve.
intro.h1: Egg-free holiday party sours to make at home
intro.texto:
Use {dose} ml of chilled VERY AQUAFABA per drink in place of egg white. For 12 holiday party sours, measure {dose_12} ml in total. Mix the spirit, citrus juice and syrup ahead, then add the aquafaba to each drink as you make it. For a Whiskey Sour, shake for {dry_shake} seconds without ice to build the foam, then add ice and shake for another {wet_shake} seconds before straining.

If you’re having friends over, whiskey sours and amaretto sours make an easy pair. Both use lemon juice, so you can squeeze the lemons before anyone arrives and shake the drinks as you serve them.

secciones.h2: How much aquafaba do you need for your party?
secciones.texto:
Count the cocktails you’ll actually shake, including any second pours you plan to offer. Multiply the number of drinks by {dose} ml. A 1L Tetrapak makes {drinks_per_litre} sours at that measure.

Set out a cocktail shaker, a jigger, a strainer and your glasses. You can measure the total for your party in advance, keep it chilled, then use the jigger to measure each drink.

secciones.h2: Which sours can you offer with one citrus?
secciones.texto:
Start with the bottles you already have. Whiskey Sour, Amaretto Sour and White Lady all use lemon juice, so any two make a short menu with one fruit to squeeze. Choose Pisco Sour if you’d like a lime option. Use each recipe for the proportions and finishing touches. Browse the Christmas cocktail recipes for a wider choice.

Amaretto SourAmarettoLemon juice

secciones.h2: What can you mix before guests arrive?
secciones.texto: Mix the spirit, citrus and syrup for each recipe in its own bottle. If you’re offering two drinks, label the bottles with the drink name and the amount of base to pour for one glass. Keep the aquafaba chilled and separate. You’ll put it straight into the shaker when you’re ready to make each drink. Use the sour batching guide when making a bottle of Pisco Sour base.

secciones.h2: How do you shake the foam when it’s time to serve?
secciones.texto:
1. Pour one serving of the base and {dose} ml of chilled VERY AQUAFABA into the shaker.
  2. Shake without ice first. This is the dry shake that builds the foam. Check the recipe for the timing.
  3. Add ice and shake again to chill and dilute the drink.
  4. Strain into the glass and serve straight away.
If the foam is thin, check whether the aquafaba went into the batch bottle or the ice went in before the first shake. For the next drink, add fresh chilled aquafaba to the shaker and do the ice-free shake first.

secciones.h2: How do you plan the rest of the pack?
secciones.texto: Liquid VERY AQUAFABA is ready to measure. Keep any opened liquid aquafaba refrigerated at {opened_temp} °C and use it within {opened_days} days. If you only make the occasional sour, you can make up just what you need from powder and measure {dose} ml of the prepared aquafaba per drink. Keep the rest of the powder dry and closed until its best-before date. Check where to buy VERY AQUAFABA before your party. Please drink responsibly.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I need for 12 sours?
faq.answer: Measure {dose_12} ml in total at {dose} ml per drink. Keep it separate from the cocktail base and add it to each shaker as you serve.

faq.question: Can I mix the aquafaba into my cocktail bottle ahead of time?
faq.answer: Keep it separate and chilled. The bottle can hold the spirit, citrus and syrup. The aquafaba goes in the shaker just before you build the foam.

faq.question: Can I dry shake my drinks before the guests arrive?
faq.answer: Shake each drink when you’re ready to pour it. You can mix the base and chill the aquafaba ahead, then do both shakes immediately before serving.

faq.question: Can I use VERY AQUAFABA powder in party sours?
faq.answer: Yes. Make it up with water first and chill it. Measure {dose} ml of the prepared aquafaba per drink.

faq.question: When do I add tonic to a Gin Fizz?
faq.answer: Add it to the glass after you’ve shaken and strained the rest of the drink.

If the liquid looks watery, simmer it gently until slightly syrupy, then chill it before whipping.

secciones.h2: Can you cook the chickpeas yourself?

The recipe uses 1.5L and simmers the chickpeas for 60 to 90 minutes, until fully cooked. Let them cool in their cooking liquid before you strain it. Check whether the strained liquid coats the spoon lightly. If it is watery, gently reduce it in a saucepan. After it cools, chill it before you whip. If you’re using the chickpeas in dinner, keep them separate when you divide up the liquid.

secciones.h2: Decide which bake to make first

Small meringues show the difference between a soft peak and the glossy, upright peaks needed for piping. Try that before you start the pavlova or melt the chocolate for mousse. Keep the containers for the next recipes labelled with their weights. If the first portion needs reducing further before it whips as expected, weigh the rest again once you’ve corrected it. You can decide then whether to open another tin, add ready-made liquid if the recipe allows it, or make one fewer dessert. The holiday quantity planner helps you update the total.

faq.question: How many cans do I need for a big holiday bake?
faq.answer: Allow roughly three to four 400g cans for the {big_bake_g}g example. The amount you drain and any reduction will affect the total.

faq.question: What sort of chickpeas should I buy?
faq.answer: Choose unsalted, unflavoured chickpeas and drain them through a fine sieve.

faq.question: What if my chickpea liquid is very thin?
faq.answer: Simmer it gently until it coats a spoon lightly, then cool and chill it before you whip it.

faq.question: Can I start with dried chickpeas?
faq.answer: Yes. Save the liquid the chickpeas simmered in, strain it and chill it. Reduce it gently first if it is too thin.

faq.question: Does reducing the liquid change how much I have for the menu?
faq.answer: Yes. Reduce gently if needed, then weigh the cooled liquid again. Use that weight when deciding how many batches you have enough to make.

faq.question: How long can I keep homemade aquafaba in the fridge?
faq.answer: Keep it in a clean airtight container at {opened_temp} °C and use it within {opened_days} days. Freeze weighed portions if you need to keep it longer.

faq.question: Can I whip thawed aquafaba for meringues?

faq.question: How should I label the portions?
faq.answer: Write the weight and freezing date on the bag or container so you can select the right number of portions for a recipe.

faq.question: Does making another dessert restart the fridge window for the carton?

intro.title: Veganuary for beginners: start with meals you know
intro.description: Start Veganuary with familiar meals and a simple week-by-week plan. Learn where aquafaba helps with eggs and how to build a plant-based cooking routine.
intro.h1: How to start Veganuary with meals you already know
intro.texto:
Start Veganuary with meals you already know. Pick one plant-based dinner, one breakfast and one dish where you’d like to try cooking without eggs. For a recipe that calls for a whipped egg white and is suited to aquafaba, start with {egg_white_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA per white. For mayonnaise, follow a recipe that uses aquafaba to help bind the oil and liquid together.

You might already make bean chilli or spaghetti with tomato sauce. Put one of those meals on the list for your first week. Adding one new recipe alongside it makes it easier to see what you’ll want to cook again.

secciones.h2: What can you cook in your first week?
secciones.texto:
Write down three meals you already make. Choose one you can make plant-based with ingredients you know, such as a bean or lentil dinner. For another, check which ingredients do the work in the recipe. Pasta with tomato sauce may only need a change to what you sprinkle on top. Pancakes need a closer look because the egg helps hold the batter together.

Check the labels on ready-made sauces, spreads and mixes if you want the whole meal to be vegan. Start with the groceries you’re likely to use again.

secciones.h2: Where does aquafaba come in?
secciones.texto:
Aquafaba is the liquid from cooking chickpeas. It can help with different jobs that eggs do. Try one job first and follow a recipe that already uses it.
If you want to learnTry
How to bind a batterA small test batch of pancakes
How to make an emulsionMayonnaise with a stick blender
How to whip a foamAn aquafaba meringue recipe
A whole-egg swap depends on the dish. Use the plant-based egg substitute guide when you need to work out whether the egg helps the mixture bind or gives the recipe its lift.

secciones.h2: How can you build on that over the month?
secciones.texto: In week two, repeat the meal you liked and try one way to cook without eggs. In week three, use a technique you’ve learnt in another recipe. By the fourth week, keep the meals and ingredients you actually want to use again. When a recipe you want to make calls for aquafaba, put it on the same list as the rest of the ingredients. If you are trying one recipe, you can start with liquid drained from unsalted, unflavoured chickpeas where the recipe allows. If you want to cook with aquafaba regularly, ready-to-measure VERY AQUAFABA saves you from matching each recipe to what you’ve drained. The Veganuary shopping list helps you choose how much to buy.

secciones.h2: What could one week look like?
secciones.texto:
Choose one dinner you already know, such as pasta with a lentil and tomato sauce. Make enough of the sauce for how your household normally eats. For breakfast, choose something familiar and check what you usually add to it. Then pick one dish that will teach you something new. If it’s pancakes, try one in the pan and see whether you like the texture before changing all your weekend breakfasts.

If the first experiment is mayonnaise, make it for a meal you already planned. Use it in a sandwich or with a potato salad and decide whether you would make it again. Next time, try a dish that uses aquafaba differently, such as small meringues. Keep the recipes you enjoyed where you can find them when you make the next shopping list.

faq.question: What if most of my usual meals contain eggs or dairy?
faq.answer: Choose one meal at a time and work out what you use the egg or dairy for. Start with a published plant-based recipe for the first dish you want to change.

faq.question: Do I need aquafaba for every plant-based meal?
faq.answer: Use it when a recipe calls for it or when it can do a specific job such as whipping, binding or emulsifying. Many plant-based meals need no egg replacement.

faq.question: What is an easy first recipe to try with aquafaba?
faq.answer: If you have a stick blender, try the mayonnaise recipe. For baking, try the meringue recipe and use its visual cues to check the foam.

faq.question: Can I make this a gradual change?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep the meals you enjoyed, repeat them and build up a small set of recipes you can cook comfortably after January.

faq.question: What if I only want to change one meal this week?
faq.answer: Start there. Choose a meal you already know, keep the part you enjoy and find a plant-based version you would happily make again.

intro.title: How to bake egg-free Christmas cookies with aquafaba

intro.h1: How do I make eggless Christmas cookies with aquafaba?

If you’re making stars or other cut-outs for a gift box, try a few of the same shape first. Once they’ve cooled, you’ll be able to see whether the edges held and the cookies are sturdy enough to pack.

secciones.h2: Check what the egg does in your dough
secciones.texto: This is a starting point for doughs where the egg holds the ingredients together. Read the mixing instructions before you swap it. For cookies made by whipping whites, use the meringue cookie recipe and its own ingredient amounts and oven settings. If you’re baking for someone who avoids eggs, check your icing, sprinkles and any bought-in pastry as well as the dough.

secciones.h2: Weigh and mix the aquafaba
secciones.texto: Measure {whole_egg_g}g per whole egg. Mix it with the sugar before adding the fat if you’re following the method for fat-rich doughs in the aquafaba baking guide. With powder, prepare it with water first, then weigh the liquid amount the recipe needs. If your original dough also calls for water or milk, try a {liquid_cut}% reduction in that added liquid as a starting point for suitable whole-egg swaps. Keep the adjustment written down so you can repeat the batch if you like the result.

secciones.h2: Bake a few cookies before you fill the tray
secciones.texto: Make a small batch and shape several cookies just as you plan to shape the rest. Use the timing and doneness cues in your recipe. Once cool, check the spread, whether the edges are still distinct and whether the cookies hold together when lifted. If you’re decorating them, wait until the cookies have cooled before adding icing. You can plan the rest of the box with the Christmas baking guide.

secciones.h2: Use the test tray to check the shape you’re giving away
secciones.texto:
If you plan to pack stars, test stars. Thin points and edges are part of how that cookie bakes. Keep the thickness and spacing from the recipe when you cut the dough, then check the outline after the cookies cool. A round tester can tell you whether the dough holds together, but it doesn’t tell you how well a narrow shape will hold up in the box.

For drop cookies, portion the test pieces the same way you’ll portion the rest. Look at the spread and how easily the cookies lift once cool. If one tray spreads more than you want, note the dough and whether the recipe called for chilling before you change anything else.

secciones.h2: Keep the dough and decoration decisions separate
secciones.texto: Before making the full batch, check the ingredients a guest would actually eat. That includes the icing or glaze and anything pressed on top. Set the cooled cookies aside before decorating so you can judge the bake on its own. If you’re preparing a mixed box, the meringue cookies use a separate whipped recipe and are easiest to keep in their own tin until packing. Write down the successful aquafaba amount and any change to the added liquid. Use that note the next time you bake the same dough. If you change to a different cookie recipe, check what its egg does before reusing the adjustment.

faq.question: How much liquid aquafaba do I use for one whole egg in cookie dough?
faq.answer: Start with {whole_egg_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA when the egg is there to bind the dough.

faq.question: Do I need to whip aquafaba for cut-out cookies?
faq.answer: Add it unwhipped when the dough uses egg for binding. Follow a whipped aquafaba recipe for meringue cookies.

faq.question: What should I look for on a test tray?
faq.answer: Check the spread and edges. Lift a cookie after it cools to see whether it holds together.

faq.question: Can I use powder in my cookie dough?

faq.question: Can I use the same method for every cookie in a gift box?
faq.answer: Check each dough. A cut-out cookie that uses egg to hold ingredients together and a piped meringue that relies on a stable foam need different methods.

intro.title: Egg-free holiday sponge cake with aquafaba
intro.description: Try aquafaba in a holiday sponge with a small test bake. Learn when to whip it, how much to measure and what to check before stacking layers.
intro.h1: How do I make an eggless sponge cake for holiday layers?
intro.texto:
For a sponge recipe suited to an aquafaba swap, start with {egg_white_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA per egg white, or {whole_egg_g}g per whole egg. If the recipe gets its lift from whipped whites, whip chilled aquafaba. For a high-sugar sponge, whip it with part of the sugar and fold gently. Try one layer before making a full cake, especially if the recipe depends on whipped whole eggs.

If you’d like a layer cake for Christmas, use the test to see how the sponge slices and whether it can hold the filling you have in mind.

secciones.h2: Read the mixing steps before you choose a swap
secciones.texto: Look for a separate step where the egg whites are whipped and folded into the batter. In that case the foam is part of what gives your sponge its lift. A génoise that gets its structure from whipped whole eggs needs a recipe-specific test. Use the aquafaba baking guide for the mixing options. For a suitable swap, weigh the aquafaba first and keep the other ingredients measured and ready so you can fold the mixture once it is whipped.

secciones.h2: Whip and fold the aquafaba
secciones.texto: Use chilled aquafaba when the recipe relies on a foam. For high-sugar batters, whip the aquafaba with part of the sugar, then fold it into the batter gently. If you’re mixing a fat-rich batter, mix the aquafaba with the sugar before you add the fat. When swapping whole eggs in a suitable recipe with separately added milk or water, try a {liquid_cut}% reduction in that added liquid as a starting point. Record the change and use the oven setting and doneness cues from your own recipe.

secciones.h2: Test the layer before you choose a filling
secciones.texto: Let the layer cool, then slice it and check the crumb. If it holds together and has the texture you want, repeat the same measurements for the other layers. A cooled sponge can be finished with aquafaba meringue buttercream. If you plan to serve it in slices with a light topping, vanilla aquafaba whipped topping can be spooned on at the table.

secciones.h2: Give the test layer the same job as the final cake
secciones.texto:
Bake the test in the shape you plan to use. A thin layer for a filled sponge needs to lift cleanly and feel sturdy enough to move. A taller cake needs enough structure to cut without breaking apart. Follow your recipe’s baking and cooling instructions so you can judge the result at the stage when you’ll actually decorate it.

Once the layer is cool, cut a slice and look at how even the crumb is. Spread a little of the planned filling on a portion before you make the rest of the layers. You can see whether it holds its shape and whether the filling works with the texture. Use the same measurements for the rest only once you’re happy with that layer.

secciones.h2: What if the cake needs more lift than a liquid swap can give?
secciones.texto: Check whether the original method asks you to whip the whole eggs until they become thick and airy. That foam is part of the design of a génoise. If the test bakes too dense, start with a sponge recipe designed for aquafaba instead of relying on the conversion alone. Keep the filling and decoration ideas while you change the base. If you’re making an assortment for Christmas, plan the layer cake alongside desserts such as mousse and pavlova so you can set aside fridge and oven time separately.

faq.question: Can I use aquafaba in a génoise?
faq.answer: Test your recipe first. Whole-egg foam does several jobs in a génoise, so bake one layer and check the lift and crumb before making a full cake.

faq.question: How much aquafaba replaces the whites in my sponge?
faq.answer: Start with {egg_white_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA per egg white. Whip it if the original recipe calls for whipped whites.

faq.question: Should I reduce the other liquid in a sponge?
faq.answer: For a suitable whole-egg swap, start by reducing separately added water or milk by {liquid_cut}%. Follow the original liquid amounts for an egg-white swap.

faq.question: Can I decorate the test layer?
faq.answer: Let it cool and check that it slices cleanly. Then try a little of the filling or frosting you plan to use on the finished cake.

faq.question: Should I check the crumb while the cake is warm?
faq.answer: Let the test layer cool first. Then cut into it and see whether it slices and holds the filling you want to use.

intro.title: Aquafaba meringue cookies for Christmas gift boxes
intro.description: Make about 30 small aquafaba meringue cookies. Learn when to add the sugar, how to tell when they’re dry and how to keep them crisp in a gift box.
intro.h1: Aquafaba meringue cookies for a Christmas cookie box
intro.texto:
Whip {meringue_g}g of chilled liquid VERY AQUAFABA with {meringue_sugar}g of caster sugar to make about {meringue_yield} small meringue cookies. Pipe 3 to 4 cm rounds and bake at {meringue_oven} °C with the fan off for {meringue_hours} hours, until completely dry. Cool them on the tray and keep them airtight until you pack the cookie boxes.

Small meringues fit easily between larger cookies. If you’re making a mixed box, keep them in their own tin until it’s time to pack so they’re still crisp when you give them away.

secciones.h2: What do you need for one tray?
secciones.texto:
IngredientAmount

Caster sugar{meringue_sugar}g

Use a clean, grease-free bowl and whisk, a piping bag and a tray lined with baking parchment. If you’re using powder, mix {meringue_powder}g with {meringue_water} ml of water for this batch.

secciones.h2: How do you whip and bake them?
secciones.texto:
Follow the VERY AQUAFABA meringue recipe and check the foam at each stage.
  1. Chill the aquafaba to {meringue_chill} °C. Whip on high speed until the foam reaches soft peaks, about {meringue_whip} minutes.
  2. If using cream of tartar or citric acid, add it while whipping.
  3. Turn the mixer to medium and add the sugar a tablespoon at a time. Let each addition dissolve before adding the next. Then increase the speed and whip until the foam is glossy and holds stiff peaks.
  4. Pipe 3 to 4 cm shapes and bake at {meringue_oven} °C with the fan off for {meringue_hours} hours. The cookies are ready when completely dry. Let them cool fully on the tray.

secciones.h2: How do you keep them crisp until you give them away?
secciones.texto: Put the cooled cookies in an airtight container at room temperature. Add a desiccant sachet if you have one. Open the tin when you’re ready to pack. If other cookies in the gift box are soft or filled, keep the meringues in a small airtight container of their own. If the cookies turn tacky or start to weep, check how well you dissolved the sugar and how tightly the tin closes. Check for moisture or undissolved sugar before packing the next batch.

secciones.h2: What should the foam look like before you pipe?
secciones.texto: Lift the whisk after the first whipping stage. The tip of a soft peak bends over. Once all the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is ready to pipe, a peak should stand upright. The foam should look glossy. A clean bowl and whisk help from the start, especially if you mixed something with butter in the same bowl earlier in the day. If the meringue starts weeping after baking, check how you added the sugar. Allow each spoonful to dissolve before adding more. If the meringues were dry but turned sticky later, check the container and how long it stayed open. Check what made the meringues sticky before you put away the next tray.

secciones.h2: Plan the gift box around the meringues
secciones.texto: A small meringue is light and can be fragile. Keep the tray of finished meringues separate while you ice other cookies or pack the heavier pieces. Once they are completely cool, move them into their airtight container. If you are giving them with softer cookies, a small separate tin or airtight container keeps them apart until the box is opened. For more trays, scale the aquafaba and caster sugar together using the meringue sugar ratio. Keep the piping size the same if you’re counting pieces for several boxes. intro.title: Folding chocolate into aquafaba for light mousse
intro.description: Learn how to cool, whip and fold chocolate into aquafaba to help your mousse keep an airy texture, with practical fixes for a dense, heavy result at home.
intro.h1: How to fold chocolate into aquafaba for a light mousse
intro.texto: When your aquafaba mousse turns dense as the chocolate goes in, melt the chocolate to 45 to 50 °C and fold it in only once it has cooled to 35 °C or lower. Hotter chocolate collapses the foam. Fold only chocolate cooled to 35 °C or lower. You can make about 6 portions with 120g of chilled aquafaba, 100g of caster sugar and 180g of dark chocolate at 70%. We make ready-made, filtered and standardised aquafaba, so you can begin with a measured ingredient rather than homemade liquid or canned chickpea water. Our 1L Tetrapak contains the equivalent of 33 egg whites for repeated mousse batches at home. The crucial moment is combining fluid chocolate with foam that has enough structure to carry it. This guide explains the temperature, peak stage and folding motion that keep the mousse light.

secciones.h2: Cool the chocolate to 35 °C
secciones.texto:
Start by melting the 180g dark chocolate gently over a bain-marie until it is smooth, at 45 to 50 °C. Then leave it until it reaches 35 °C or lower before it comes near the bowl of foam.

If it is still hot, wait rather than trying to fold faster. Hot chocolate collapses the foam.

secciones.h2: Whip the foam to glossy stiff peaks
secciones.texto:
Use 120g of chilled aquafaba, the equivalent of 4 egg whites in these mousse quantities. Whip it to soft peaks for 3 to 4 minutes, then add 100g of caster sugar gradually. Keep whipping until the foam reaches glossy stiff peaks.

The peak should stand when you lift the whisk, rather than drooping back into the bowl. You need this structure before the chocolate enters, because folding releases some air. Cream of tartar, 2g, or citric acid, 1g, is optional. Add either before whipping if you use it, then judge the foam by its stiff, glossy peak rather than the clock alone.

secciones.h2: Fold quickly and lightly
secciones.texto:
Move without delay once the chocolate and foam are ready. Fold the cooled chocolate into the foam with a spatula, quickly and lightly. Stop as soon as it is combined.

Beating or stirring in circles presses out the air you built during whipping. For a larger batch, mix part of the chocolate with a little aquafaba first. You then fold that lighter chocolate mixture into the remaining foam. This can make the chocolate easier to introduce without dropping all of it directly onto the full bowl of foam.

secciones.h2: Try it on your next mousse
secciones.texto:
Portion the mousse once the chocolate is evenly folded, then chill it at 4 °C for at least 2 hours. The recipe quantities make about 6 portions. Keep any remaining mousse sealed in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

If you are preparing ahead, finish the folding before portioning so you do not keep working the foam. For your next batch, use the same temperature check and peak test before changing the flavouring or serving size. We offer a 200g powder pouch, the equivalent of 100 egg whites, and a 1L Tetrapak, the equivalent of 33 egg whites, for home mousse making.

faq.question: Why did I get a dense aquafaba mousse?
faq.answer: You may have added chocolate above 35 °C, or stopped whipping before the foam reached glossy stiff peaks. You need both checks in place because hot chocolate collapses the foam and softer foam has less structure for folding.

faq.question: Can I fold chocolate in while it is warmer than 35 °C?
faq.answer: You should not fold chocolate in while it is warmer than 35 °C. Let it cool to 35 °C or lower, then begin folding while it is still fluid.

faq.question: Should I stop whipping at soft peaks?
faq.answer: You should not stop at soft peaks. You first whip chilled aquafaba to soft peaks, add caster sugar gradually, then continue until you have glossy stiff peaks.

faq.question: How do I fold chocolate into aquafaba for a large batch?
faq.answer: You should first mix part of the chocolate with a little aquafaba. You then fold that mixture into the rest of your foam, rather than adding all the chocolate directly.

faq.question: How long can I keep my finished mousse?
faq.answer: You should chill your finished mousse at 4 °C for at least 2 hours before serving. Keep it sealed in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

end.cierre: Set out a thermometer and spatula before you melt the chocolate, then prepare the foam until its peak stands glossy and stiff. Fold the cooled chocolate in only until it is combined, then chill the portions. For your next mousse, order the 200g pouch or the 1L Tetrapak online from Amazon in the United States, Germany and Austria, InstantChef in France, Siradis in Switzerland or Qualifirst in Canada.

intro.title: Egg-free Christmas macarons for homemade gift boxes
intro.description: Make about 40 egg-free Christmas macarons with VERY AQUAFABA. Bake the shells, choose festive fillings and refrigerate overnight before packing your gift boxes.
intro.h1: Christmas macarons for homemade gift boxes, without eggs
intro.texto:
You can make around {macarons} egg-free Christmas macarons using {liquid_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA in place of {egg_whites} egg whites, along with caster sugar, almond flour and icing sugar. Bake the shells at {bake} °C for {bake_time} minutes with the fan off. Fill and refrigerate the macarons for {mature} hours before packing them into Christmas gift boxes so the texture can develop.

For a mixed gift box, make one batch of almond shells and vary the fillings. Choose the fillings with the person receiving the box in mind.

secciones.h2: Ingredients for {macarons} Christmas macarons
secciones.texto:
The following quantities make around {shells} shells, or {macarons} filled macarons, using the VERY AQUAFABA macaron recipe.
IngredientQuantity
Liquid VERY AQUAFABA{liquid_g}g
Caster sugar{sugar}g
Almond flour{almond}g
Icing sugar{icing_sugar}g
Cream of tartar or citric acid, optional2g cream of tartar or 1g citric acid
Food colouringOptional
Filling of your choiceAbout 300g
If you're using VERY AQUAFABA powder instead of liquid, mix {powder_g}g of powder with {water_ml} ml of water. Set out a mixer, a clean, grease-free bowl and whisk, a sieve, a spatula and a piping bag with a plain round tip. Line the baking trays with baking parchment.

secciones.h2: How to make egg-free macaron shells
secciones.texto:
1. Sift the almond flour and icing sugar together.
  2. Whip the chilled aquafaba on high speed until soft peaks form. If you’re using an optional stabiliser, add it at this stage.
  3. Gradually add the caster sugar and continue whipping until the meringue is glossy and holds stiff peaks.
  4. Fold the dry ingredients into the meringue in three additions, until the batter falls from the spatula in thick ribbons.
  5. Pipe rounds measuring 3 to 4 cm onto your baking trays.
  6. Leave the shells to rest for {rest} minutes, until a skin forms on the surface.
  7. Bake at {bake} °C for {bake_time} minutes with the fan off.
  8. Allow the shells to cool completely before lifting them from the tray.

secciones.h2: Which fillings will you put in the box?
secciones.texto:
Bake one batch of almond shells and vary the filling across the box. The recipe takes any of four:
  • Ganache
  • Buttercream
  • Jam
  • Fruit compote
Pair the shells by size first, so each macaron sits level in the box. Pipe the filling onto one shell and press the second gently on top. Fill each flavour as its own group, then mix them when you pack. If you’re avoiding animal ingredients, check what goes into each filling.

secciones.h2: When should you make macarons for Christmas?
secciones.texto:
Work backwards from the time you want to pack or serve the macarons. The filled macarons need a full day in the fridge.
WhenWhat to do
Before bakingPrepare your ingredients, fillings and gift boxes.
The day before giftingBake the shells and let them cool. Pair them by size, pipe the filling onto one shell in each pair and gently press the shells together.
During the following {mature} hoursRefrigerate the filled macarons to let the texture develop.
On the day of giftingArrange the macarons in their boxes and add your finishing touches.

secciones.h2: Choosing aquafaba for your Christmas baking
secciones.texto: Liquid VERY AQUAFABA is ready to use. A 1L Tetrapak contains enough aquafaba for around {batches_1l} batches. If you’re planning several gift boxes, the macaron quantity calculator scales the shell ingredients for you. Once opened, keep liquid aquafaba refrigerated at {opened_temp} °C and use it within {opened_days} days. Powder is a convenient alternative if you bake less frequently. You can prepare the quantity you need and keep the remaining powder dry and sealed until its best-before date. Both formats keep for at least {unopened_months} months at room temperature before opening. Plan the rest of your Christmas baking without eggs while you set the macarons aside to mature. Check where to buy VERY AQUAFABA for your holiday baking before you shop for your fillings and gift boxes.

faq.question: Can I make Christmas macarons with aquafaba powder?
faq.answer: Yes. Mix {powder_g}g of VERY AQUAFABA powder with {water_ml} ml of water and follow the same method for whipping, folding, piping and baking the shells.

faq.question: How far in advance should I fill macarons for Christmas?
faq.answer: Fill your macarons {mature} hours before you plan to pack or serve them. Refrigerate them for the full {mature} hours so the texture can develop.

faq.question: Why do my macaron shells need to rest before baking?
faq.answer: Resting allows a skin to form on the surface of the piped batter. Leave the shells for {rest} minutes and check that this skin has formed before putting them into the oven.

faq.question: Which fillings can I use?
faq.answer: Ganache, buttercream, jam or fruit compote. If you’re avoiding animal ingredients, check what goes into each one. Check any chocolate, buttercream and icing you buy. The shells contain almonds.

faq.question: What can I do with leftover aquafaba after making macarons?
faq.answer: You can use the remaining aquafaba in other recipes, such as meringues, chocolate mousse or cocktails. Keep opened liquid VERY AQUAFABA refrigerated at {opened_temp} °C and use it within {opened_days} days.

intro.title: Egg-free Christmas pavlova you can make ahead
intro.description: Bake an egg-free Christmas pavlova base the day before with {aquafaba_g}g of VERY AQUAFABA. Keep it crisp overnight and top it with cream and fruit just before serving.
intro.h1: Egg-free Christmas pavlova you can make ahead
intro.texto: Bake one {diameter_cm} cm egg-free Christmas pavlova base the day before serving. Whip {aquafaba_g}g of chilled liquid VERY AQUAFABA with {sugar_g}g of caster sugar, fold in {cornstarch_g}g of corn starch and {vinegar_g}g of white wine vinegar or lemon juice, then bake at {oven_c} °C with the fan off for {bake_hours} hours. Let it cool completely in the switched-off oven with the door ajar, then store the plain shell in an airtight container with a desiccant sachet. Add the cream and fruit just before serving.

secciones.h2: What you need for one pavlova
secciones.texto:
IngredientAmount
Chilled liquid VERY AQUAFABA{aquafaba_g}g
Caster sugar{sugar_g}g
Corn starch{cornstarch_g}g
Cream of tartar or citric acid, optional{cream_of_tartar_g}g cream of tartar or {citric_acid_g}g citric acid
White wine vinegar or lemon juice{vinegar_g}g
Whipped plant-based cream{cream_ml} ml
Fresh fruit{fruit_g}g
Have a clean, grease-free bowl and whisk, a mixer, a spatula and a baking tray lined with baking parchment ready. The VERY AQUAFABA pavlova recipe uses aquafaba chilled to {chill_c} °C.

secciones.h2: How to bake a crisp shell with a soft centre
secciones.texto:
1. Whip the chilled aquafaba on high speed until soft peaks form. If using the optional cream of tartar or citric acid, add it now and continue whipping until the peaks firm up.
  2. Add the caster sugar gradually while whipping. The meringue is ready for the next step when it looks glossy and the peaks stand upright.
  3. Gently fold in the corn starch and the white wine vinegar or lemon juice. Both go in even if you used an optional stabiliser.
  4. Spoon the meringue onto the lined tray. Shape it into a {diameter_cm} cm disc with a slightly raised rim to hold the cream and fruit.
  5. Bake at {oven_c} °C with the fan off for {bake_hours} hours. Look for a crisp outside with a centre that stays slightly soft.
  6. Switch off the oven and leave the shell inside with the door ajar. Let it cool completely there. Gradual cooling helps prevent cracks.

secciones.h2: How to keep the base crisp overnight
secciones.texto: If you’re serving the pavlova on Christmas Day, start on Christmas Eve with enough time for both the bake and the oven cooling. Once the shell is completely cool, put it in an airtight container with a desiccant sachet. Keep the toppings separate until you’re ready to serve. Moisture from the cream and fruit would soften the shell if you added them ahead.

secciones.h2: How to finish your Christmas pavlova
secciones.texto: Put the shell on its serving plate before you spoon the whipped plant-based cream inside the rim. Scatter the fruit over the cream and serve straight away. Use {fruit_g}g of fresh seasonal fruit in all, and leave some of the white cream showing.

secciones.h2: What to do with the rest of the carton
secciones.texto: If you’re baking several holiday desserts, use the leftover aquafaba for Christmas macarons or chocolate mousse. Keep opened liquid VERY AQUAFABA in the fridge at {opened_temp} °C and use it within {opened_days} days. Check where to buy VERY AQUAFABA for holiday baking before you plan your baking day.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake the pavlova base?
faq.answer: Bake it one day ahead. Cool it completely in the switched-off oven with the door ajar, then store it airtight with a desiccant sachet until assembly.

faq.question: What should the meringue look like before I shape it?
faq.answer: After you’ve added the sugar, look for glossy, stiff peaks. The tip should stand up when you lift the whisk. Fold in the corn starch and vinegar or lemon juice gently at that point.

faq.question: Can I use lemon juice in place of white wine vinegar?
faq.answer: Yes. Use {vinegar_g}g of lemon juice in place of the white wine vinegar and fold it in with the corn starch.

faq.question: Do I need cream of tartar for this pavlova?
faq.answer: It’s optional. If you want to use a stabiliser, add {cream_of_tartar_g}g of cream of tartar or {citric_acid_g}g of citric acid after the aquafaba reaches soft peaks.

faq.question: What cream can I use for a plant-based topping?
faq.answer: Use whipped plant-based cream and fresh fruit. Check the ingredients in any additional decorations you plan to add.

intro.title: Egg-free Christmas cocktails with aquafaba foam
intro.description: Choose a Christmas cocktail by flavour and make its foam without egg white. Browse seven recipes that use 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink.
intro.h1: How to make Christmas cocktails with egg white-style foam
intro.texto:
Use {dose} ml of chilled VERY AQUAFABA per drink for an egg-free foam on Christmas cocktails. Dry shake the aquafaba with the cocktail base, shake again with ice, then strain. Choose the recipe for the spirit, citrus and finish you like, and add any fizzy top-up after straining.

If you already have amaretto in the cupboard, start there. For something lighter and longer, try a Gin Fizz with tonic. You can pick one recipe to make on the night and keep the ingredients list short.

secciones.h2: How do you get a fresh layer of foam?
secciones.texto:
Use a jigger to measure {dose} ml of chilled aquafaba for each recipe. Shake with the base before adding ice, then shake again after you’ve added the ice. The whiskey sour recipe specifies {dry_shake} seconds for the first shake and {wet_shake} seconds for the second. Use the instructions for the drink you’ve chosen.

For a Gin Fizz or The Sunset, leave the carbonated part out of the shaker. Add it to the glass after you strain the drink.

secciones.h2: What can you get ready before friends arrive?
secciones.texto: Get the glasses, jigger and strainer out and chill the aquafaba. If you’re making several drinks, use the holiday party sours guide to work out how much base and aquafaba you’ll need.

secciones.h2: Choose a short menu from the ingredients you have
secciones.texto:
If you already have gin and lemons, decide whether you want a short drink with orange liqueur or a longer one topped with tonic. If you have amaretto, the sour uses lemon and vanilla syrup, while The Sunset also needs rum and ginger beer. A two-drink menu can work if both drinks use ingredients you’ll finish. Use the linked recipes to see what else goes into each one.

Check the garnish and glass in the recipe you pick before you buy anything extra. A short sour and a longer fizzy drink will also need different glasses. When you’re serving both, set the glasses out together and keep each recipe’s ingredients beside them.

secciones.h2: Get the drink’s finish right
secciones.texto: Shake the foam fresh before you pour. If you’re making whiskey sours, the recipe’s optional bitters sit on the foam, where you can swirl them with a cocktail pick. For a long drink, strain the shaken ingredients first and add the fizz to the glass afterwards. Keep the tonic or ginger beer ready so you can finish as soon as you’ve strained it. If friends want different drinks, choose each base ahead and avoid mixing their garnishes and top-ups together. Use the holiday party sours quantities for the amount of aquafaba you’ll need once you know how many glasses you’re serving. Please drink responsibly.

faq.question: Can I make Christmas cocktails with foam without using egg white?
faq.answer: Yes. Measure {dose} ml of chilled VERY AQUAFABA for each drink and dry shake it with your cocktail base before adding ice.

faq.question: What’s a Christmas cocktail I can make with amaretto?
faq.answer: Try an Amaretto Sour for a short drink with lemon and vanilla, or The Sunset for a longer rum and amaretto drink topped with ginger beer.

faq.question: When do I add tonic or ginger beer?
faq.answer: Pour it into the glass once you’ve shaken and strained the rest of the drink.

faq.question: Can I decorate the foam on a whiskey sour?
faq.answer: The recipe suggests a drop or two of bitters, swirled on the foam with a cocktail pick.

faq.question: Which Christmas cocktail is easy to make if I already have gin and lemons?
faq.answer: Try the Gin Fizz if you also have tonic, or the White Lady if you have orange liqueur. Follow the chosen recipe for the exact amounts.

intro.title: Egg-free coconut marshmallows for holiday gifts
intro.description: Make egg-free coconut marshmallows with whipped aquafaba and iota carrageenan. Get the ingredient weights, syrup temperatures and toasted coconut finish.
intro.h1: Vegan marshmallows recipe with toasted coconut
intro.texto:
Use {aquafaba_g}g of VERY AQUAFABA for one frame of egg-free coconut marshmallows. Cook the syrup to {syrup_c} °C, use it at {syrup_cool_c} °C and prepare the iota carrageenan gel at {gel_c} °C. Let the marshmallows set in the frame before you cut them and roll the pieces in toasted coconut.

If you’re giving them away, leave yourself time to let the slab set before cutting and packing it. A small box of coconut-covered pieces is an easy addition to a homemade gift.

secciones.h2: What do you need for one frame?
secciones.texto:
Part of the recipeIngredients
Foam{aquafaba_g}g liquid VERY AQUAFABA
Syrup{syrup_water_g}g water, {syrup_sugar_g}g sugar and {invert_sugar_g}g invert sugar

Coconut{coconut_total_g}g to toast, including {coconut_in_mix_g}g for the mixture
Set out a thermometer, a scale, a mixer and a frame on a silicone mat. Weigh the syrup and gel ingredients separately so they’re ready when you start heating.

secciones.h2: Which temperatures do you need to check?
secciones.texto: The syrup reaches {syrup_c} °C during cooking and is added at {syrup_cool_c} °C. Prepare the iota carrageenan gel at {gel_c} °C. A thermometer helps you keep the three stages straight. Follow the mixing order in the full coconut marshmallow recipe when combining the whipped aquafaba, syrup and gel. Have the frame ready before you mix. Whisk the iota carrageenan and sugar into the gel water, then heat to {gel_c} °C. Add the gel to the syrup once the syrup is at {syrup_cool_c} °C. Pour the mixture gradually over the whipped aquafaba with the mixer running and add the portion of toasted coconut. Before pouring, get the frame and toasted coconut ready. Have another look at the marshmallow temperatures and order of mixing so you can follow them while the syrup is hot.

secciones.h2: How do you finish the marshmallows?
secciones.texto: Toast the coconut at {toast_c} °C for {toast_minutes} minutes with the fan on. Use {coconut_in_mix_g}g in the mixture and keep the coconut for coating aside. Let the slab set, cut it into pieces and roll the cut pieces in the toasted coconut. If you’re giving pieces away, say that they contain coconut and list the other ingredients on the box. For more than one frame, use the marshmallow quantity calculator before you weigh the ingredients.

secciones.h2: Set up the frame before you heat anything
secciones.texto:
Put the frame on the silicone mat and clear room for it beside the mixing bowl. Keep the ingredients for the syrup, gel and foam in separate groups. A kitchen scale helps you keep the small carrageenan amount apart from the two sugar measures. Have the thermometer ready to check the hot syrup and gel. Use the temperature for the particular stage you’re working on before you combine anything.

When the coconut is toasted, weigh what goes into the mixture and set the rest aside for coating. That way you’re ready to roll the cut pieces later and won’t have to guess which part to save when the syrup is already heating.

secciones.h2: Give the pieces time to set before packing
secciones.texto: Leave the slab in the frame until it has set. You should be able to lift and handle the cut pieces well enough to roll them in the toasted coconut. If the slab stays soft and sticky, the syrup came off the heat before {syrup_c} °C. Check the thermometer before you cook the next batch. Keep the coated pieces in an airtight tin in a dry place, and pack them only once they have cooled completely. For gifts, keep the ingredient information with the box. List the coconut alongside the other ingredients. If you’re also making small meringues or filled macarons, pack those according to their own handling instructions. Work out the number of frames you want before multiplying your shopping quantities. One frame takes {aquafaba_g}g, so once the 1L Tetrapak is open, keep the rest at {opened_temp} °C and use it within {opened_days} days, or freeze it in weighed portions.

faq.question: Do I need a thermometer for these marshmallows?
faq.answer: Yes. Check the syrup at {syrup_c} °C for cooking and {syrup_cool_c} °C for adding it. The gel has its own {gel_c} °C checkpoint.

faq.question: How much aquafaba goes in one frame?
faq.answer: Use {aquafaba_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for one frame.

faq.question: How much toasted coconut goes into the mixture?
faq.answer: Weigh out {coconut_in_mix_g}g for the mixture and set aside toasted coconut for rolling the pieces.

faq.question: When can I cut the marshmallows?
faq.answer: Wait until the slab has set in the frame, then cut and coat the pieces.

faq.question: Can I toast the coconut while the syrup is cooking?
faq.answer: It is easier to toast and weigh the coconut before you start the syrup, so you can watch the temperature checkpoints without having to measure anything else.

intro.title: Egg-free brioche and holiday sweet rolls with aquafaba
intro.description: Try VERY AQUAFABA in brioche or sweet roll dough, check the liquid adjustment and bake a small batch before making a full tray for the holidays.
intro.h1: Eggless brioche and sweet rolls for the holidays
intro.texto: For enriched dough suited to an egg swap, start with {whole_egg_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA per whole egg. Add it with the liquids without whipping. If your recipe adds milk or water separately, start by reducing that liquid by {liquid_cut}% and test a small batch of brioche or sweet rolls. If you’re planning cinnamon rolls for a holiday breakfast, try a small batch with the filling you’ll actually use. Check the crumb once the rolls are baked and cool enough to pull apart.

secciones.h2: What does the egg contribute to an enriched dough?
secciones.texto:
Whole eggs help bind the dough and contribute moisture and richness. Aquafaba can help with binding and moisture. Try it in your recipe with its usual flour, sugar and fat so you can judge the swap.

If you’re baking for someone who avoids eggs, check the filling and any glaze as well as the dough. If you want the buns to be vegan, the milk and butter also need suitable alternatives.

secciones.h2: Where does the aquafaba go in the bowl?
secciones.texto:
Weigh {whole_egg_g}g per whole egg. Add the aquafaba when your recipe adds the liquids, then follow its own mixing, kneading and rising steps. For three eggs in a suitable dough, start with {three_eggs_g}g of liquid.

If you are using powder, prepare the mixture in a separate bowl and weigh the recipe’s dose before you add it to the dough.

secciones.h2: What should you look for in the test batch?
secciones.texto: Bake the test rolls all the way through using your recipe’s oven setting and doneness cues. Once they cool, pull one apart and check how the crumb holds together. Write down your liquid adjustment so you can repeat it. If the original recipe brushes egg on the tops, use a light aquafaba wash at the same point.

secciones.h2: Set up one small bake you can repeat
secciones.texto:
Keep the flour, yeast and fat in the first test the same as in your usual recipe. If you are rolling the dough around a filling, use the filling you actually plan to serve. Write down how much aquafaba went in and any change you made to separately added milk or water. Use the recipe’s own mixer, rise and baking directions to give the comparison a useful starting point.

For a holiday breakfast, test the rolls in the shape you want to serve. A roll should pull apart the way you like once it cools, and the filling should sit where you put it. If the crumb is denser than you want, check how the original recipe uses the eggs and whether it suits this swap before making a second full tray.

secciones.h2: Check the tops and fillings as well as the dough
secciones.texto: If your recipe calls for egg wash on the shaped dough, a light aquafaba pastry wash is a separate step. Use a brush and look for a light, even coat. For a plant-based finish, check the original butter, milk, filling and glaze. The amount of aquafaba you use to bind the dough doesn’t tell you whether those other parts of the recipe are plant-based. Keep the quantities for dough and wash on separate lines when you total up the rest of your Christmas baking.

faq.question: Do I whip aquafaba before adding it to brioche dough?
faq.answer: Add it unwhipped with the other liquid ingredients.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I use for three whole eggs in sweet rolls?
faq.answer: For a dough suited to the swap, start with {three_eggs_g}g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA and test a small batch.

faq.question: Do I change the milk in the recipe?
faq.answer: If you’re replacing whole eggs and the recipe adds milk or water separately, start by reducing that added liquid by {liquid_cut}%.

faq.question: Can I brush my rolls with aquafaba as well?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a pastry brush to apply a thin coat of liquid aquafaba before baking.

faq.question: What should I write down from my test batch?
faq.answer: Record the aquafaba weight, how much separately added liquid you held back and what the crumb looked like after cooling.

intro.title: Aquafaba egg wash for holiday pastry
intro.description: Brush liquid VERY AQUAFABA onto pie lids, brioche or pastries before baking. Learn how much to pour and how to keep the coat light and even.
intro.h1: What is a vegan egg wash substitute for pastry?
intro.texto:
Brush a thin coat of liquid VERY AQUAFABA onto shaped pastry or sweet rolls at the point your recipe calls for its wash. Pour a little into a bowl, use it straight from the pack and brush on only enough to cover the surface lightly. You can use it without whisking.

If you’re making a pie for Christmas, keep the brush beside the tray. A small pour is usually all you need to finish the lid before it goes into the oven.

secciones.h2: How do you brush a pastry lid or rolls?

secciones.h2: Use the wash at the point your recipe calls for it

intro.title: Aquafaba whipped topping for holiday desserts
intro.description: Whip chilled aquafaba to soft peaks for a spoonable topping. Learn to recognise the texture and when to add it to mousse or fruit.
intro.h1: How do I make aquafaba whipped cream for holiday desserts?
intro.texto: Whip chilled liquid VERY AQUAFABA to soft peaks for a spoonable topping. Add vanilla or icing sugar only as directed by the topping recipe you’re using. Soft peaks bend at the tip when you lift the whisk. For the Christmas pavlova, follow its recipe for whipped plant-based cream. A spoonful is enough to finish a cup of chocolate mousse or a bowl of berries. If dessert is already made, you can whip this while you’re getting the bowls out.

secciones.h2: What do you need to start whipping?
secciones.texto: Set out a clean, grease-free bowl and an electric mixer. Chill the liquid aquafaba and measure the amount your recipe specifies. Keep any stabiliser and flavourings separate so you can add them at the stage the recipe gives. Use the egg replacer whipping method to recognise soft peaks. The soft topping is for spooning at the table. If a dessert calls for plant-based cream or a frosting that holds a shape, use the topping named in that recipe.

secciones.h2: How do you tell when the foam is ready?
secciones.texto: Lift the whisk as you whip. If the foam forms a peak and the tip bends over, you’ve reached soft peaks. If it is still loose, continue following your recipe’s whipping stage and check again. Keep the vanilla and icing sugar separate until the recipe calls for them. For a familiar comparison, the small-meringue recipe has a separate stage later on for glossy, upright peaks. A soft topping doesn’t need that same end point.

secciones.h2: When should you whip it for dessert?
secciones.texto: Whip the topping close to serving and spoon it over the portions you’re about to eat. If you’re making chocolate mousse ahead, cover and chill the cups on their own. Bring them out once they’ve set and add the topping when you serve. Arrange fresh fruit or another decoration at the table if you want to give people a choice. Read the topping recipe for any preparation or storage instructions before you make it in advance.

secciones.h2: Check the peak before you add the flavour
secciones.texto: When you lift the whisk, look for a peak with a tip that falls back gently. The topping should be fluffy and easy to spoon. If the mixture is still too loose to make a peak, keep following the whipping stage before adding sugar and vanilla. Use the recipe’s timing as a guide and the peak as the check. Check the shape of the peak before moving to the flavourings. If your topping recipe lists a stabiliser, measure it before you start. Keep the vanilla and icing sugar beside it separately, ready for the final short whip.

secciones.h2: Choose a dessert you can finish with a spoon
secciones.texto: This topping is useful where you can add a spoonful just before serving. Try it on individual mousse cups or put it in a bowl beside sliced fruit. If the dessert is already cold and covered, keep it that way until you bring it out. Whip the topping near serving time if you want to see the freshest texture. If you want to decorate a cake in advance, choose a frosting intended for that job. The meringue buttercream uses a different preparation and is meant to be spread or piped onto cooled cakes. Save the soft aquafaba topping for spooning over portions. For a dessert with more than one topping, set out the fruit or grated chocolate first. Add the soft foam from the bowl when the portions are ready to eat. You can also leave it in a serving bowl so people can spoon on the amount they want.

faq.question: What does a soft peak look like?
faq.answer: The foam holds a peak when you lift the whisk, but the tip bends over. Add the sugar and vanilla at that stage.

faq.question: Can I use it to finish chocolate mousse?
faq.answer: Yes. Spoon a dollop onto the chilled mousse when you’re ready to serve it.

faq.question: Should I whip this to the same peaks as meringue cookies?
faq.answer: Look for soft peaks in this topping. The peak bends at the tip, whereas meringue cookies are piped from a foam that holds a stiff peak.

faq.question: Can I whip powder straight from the pouch?

faq.question: Can I spoon this on before the mousse has set?

faq.question: What if I need a topping that can be piped onto cupcakes?
faq.answer: Use a frosting recipe that’s intended for piping. Save this soft foam for spooning over a serving.

intro.title: Aquafaba Meringue for Pie: Lemon Topping
intro.description: Make aquafaba meringue for pie with clear quantities, spreading, setting and browning steps, plus practical guidance for serving lemon pie on the day.
intro.h1: How do I make aquafaba meringue for pie?
intro.texto: 150g of VERY AQUAFABA whipped with 150g of caster sugar tops a lemon meringue pie: spread it to the edges, set it 5 minutes in the oven and brown it with a torch. Whip the chilled liquid to soft peaks, add the sugar gradually, then take it to glossy stiff peaks before spooning it over the lemon filling. The topping method follows the vegan lemon meringue pie published by Fooduzzi. VERY AQUAFABA gives you ready-made, filtered and standardised chickpea cooking water, so you can measure the topping instead of working from cans or homemade liquid. The 1L Tetrapak contains the equivalent of 33 egg whites, and the 200g pouch contains the equivalent of 100 egg whites. Add the caster sugar 1 tablespoon at a time, allowing each addition to dissolve before the next. This guide takes you from whipping the meringue to serving the pie.

secciones.h2: The meringue for one pie
secciones.texto: Measure 150g of chilled VERY AQUAFABA and 150g of caster sugar for the meringue. Chill the aquafaba to 4 °C, then whip on high speed until soft peaks form, about 3 to 5 minutes. Change to medium speed and add the sugar 1 tablespoon at a time, letting it dissolve before you add more. Then whip until the foam is glossy and holds stiff peaks. Cream of tartar is optional: you can use 2g, or use 1g of citric acid instead. The 1L Tetrapak provides 33 egg whites of ready-made liquid for baking beyond this pie.

secciones.h2: Spread it to the edges
secciones.texto: Once the meringue is at stiff peaks, spoon it over your lemon filling while it is in the pie case. Make sure the meringue touches every side of the case. This is the edge-to-edge coverage used for the lemon pie topping, rather than leaving an exposed ring of filling. Use the back of your spoon to draw up peaks across the surface. Keep the layer in place as you shape it, so the surface is ready for the short oven set and final browning.

secciones.h2: Set it, then brown it
secciones.texto: Put the topped pie in the oven for 5 minutes to set the surface. After that short bake, brown the meringue with a kitchen torch. You can instead brown it under the grill for the last minute. Keep the peaks visible as you brown the top, and watch the surface rather than walking away from it. The oven stage is for setting. The torch or grill stage is the final browning step. You use either browning method after the initial oven set, not both. This keeps the order clear for your pie.

secciones.h2: Serve it the same day
secciones.texto: Plan to serve lemon meringue pie on the day you make it. The base turns watery overnight, so this topping suits a same-day dessert rather than a pie you assemble for tomorrow. Time the meringue around the meal or gathering when you want to cut the pie. Whip it, spread it to the edges, set it and brown it as part of the final stretch of baking. Put the finished pie on the table that day, while the base still has the texture you made it for.

faq.question: How much aquafaba meringue do I need for my pie?
faq.answer: You need 150g of chilled VERY AQUAFABA and 150g of caster sugar for the topping. You whip the aquafaba to soft peaks before adding the sugar gradually and finishing at glossy stiff peaks.

faq.question: Can I make my aquafaba meringue without cream of tartar?
faq.answer: You can make the meringue without cream of tartar. You may add 2g of cream of tartar or 1g of citric acid if you want an optional aid for foam stability.

faq.question: How do I stop my aquafaba meringue from weeping?
faq.answer: You need to add the caster sugar 1 tablespoon at a time while the mixer runs on medium speed. You let each addition dissolve before adding more, because undissolved sugar can make the meringue weep.

faq.question: Can I brown my pie topping under the grill?
faq.answer: You can brown the meringue under the grill for the last minute. You set the topped pie in the oven for 5 minutes before you use the grill.

faq.question: Can I serve my lemon meringue pie the next day?
faq.answer: You should serve the pie on the day you make it. You should expect the base to turn watery overnight.

intro.title: Aquafaba meringue buttercream for Christmas cakes

It should hold the finish you’re trying to make. If you’re frosting a holiday sponge cake, let the layers cool before you spread or pipe it.

secciones.h2: Get the bowl and baking block ready first
secciones.texto:
Set out the whisk, bowl and saucepan before you start. Weigh the aquafaba and sugar together and cut the room-temperature baking block into pieces for adding later. If you will pipe the frosting, have the piping bag ready on the counter. Make sure the cake or cupcakes have cooled by the time you finish mixing.

Check that the sugar has dissolved during the warming stage. Once you take the bowl off the heat, keep whipping until the foam is glossy, stiff and cool. A bowl that still feels warm tells you that the meringue needs more time before you add the baking block.

If you’re planning a layer cake, set out the filling and frosting bowls separately. Check whether the recipe you’ve chosen is meant to cover the outside, go between the layers or do both. That affects how much you will need before you start whipping.

secciones.h2: Check the texture before you spread or pipe it
secciones.texto: Add the baking block gradually. The mixture can look loose when the first pieces go in. Once the full amount is in the bowl, use the low-speed whisking stage and watch for a lighter, fluffier texture. If you are using frosting made ahead, let it soften before judging its texture. Follow your recipe’s handling instructions if you plan to prepare it in advance. Spoon a little onto one cooled cupcake first. If you like the finish, repeat it on the others. You can make a small swirl with a spoon or pipe a more even top with a bag. For a layer cake, start with the holiday sponge guide and check that the cooled layers hold together before frosting.

faq.question: How do I know when to add the baking block?
faq.answer: The whipped meringue should be stiff, glossy and completely cool. Add room-temperature pieces a little at a time.

faq.question: Can I pipe this onto Christmas cupcakes?
faq.answer: Yes. Wait until the cupcakes cool, then pipe the buttercream or spread it with the back of a spoon.

faq.question: Can I frost the cupcakes as soon as they come out of the oven?
faq.answer: Cool the cupcakes completely before applying the buttercream. Use the time while they cool to get the baking block and mixing equipment ready.

faq.question: How do I know a cake is ready to frost?
faq.answer: Let the layers cool completely before you spread or pipe the buttercream. Check that the sponge holds together when you move it.

faq.question: Can I use a spoon instead of a piping bag?
faq.answer: Yes. For a simple finish on cupcakes, spread the frosting with the back of a spoon once the cakes have cooled.

faq.question: How can I check how much frosting I need?

intro.title: What is in chickpea water?
intro.description: Find out what aquafaba is, what is in VERY AQUAFABA liquid and how to read the ingredients on a tin of chickpeas before you use the liquid.
intro.h1: What is in chickpea water and ready-made aquafaba?
intro.texto:
Chickpea water is the liquid left from cooking chickpeas. It contains substances from the beans, including starches and proteins, that help it whip or mix into a recipe. Liquid VERY AQUAFABA is made from water and chickpeas. For canned chickpeas, check the label for any additional ingredients.

If you’re saving a tin’s liquid for a sweet recipe, take a quick look at the ingredients first. Unsalted, unflavoured chickpeas are the starting point for the homemade aquafaba method.

secciones.h2: What gives the liquid its texture?
secciones.texto: Some of the chickpeas’ soluble proteins, starches and fibres go into the water as they cook. That is why the liquid may feel slightly thick. Once whipped, it can hold air in a recipe such as meringue. The look and thickness can vary with canned chickpeas. If you are trying to bake with it, check the consistency before you whip it.

secciones.h2: What should you check on the label?
secciones.texto:
The ingredient list for liquid VERY AQUAFABA names water and chickpeas. If you’re using a tin, read its ingredient list for seasonings or other additions. Anyone who needs to avoid chickpeas should check the product’s suitability. Also check the other ingredients in the dish.

If you’re choosing a pack for a particular recipe, check whether it is ready-made liquid or powder to be mixed with water.

secciones.h2: Where can you use what you’ve drained?
secciones.texto: Weigh the liquid before you decide. Choose a recipe that fits the amount you have or refrigerate or freeze it for later.

secciones.h2: Does every source of aquafaba contain the same things?
secciones.texto: Start with the ingredient list. A tin made with water and chickpeas is one place to get the liquid. A different tin may have seasonings or other ingredients. These may matter if you want to use the liquid in a dessert or cook for someone who needs to avoid an ingredient. For ready-made liquid VERY AQUAFABA, the ingredient list is water and chickpeas. When you buy VERY AQUAFABA powder, make it up with water: {powder_white_g}g of powder plus {powder_white_water} ml of water make {prepared_white_g}g. The liquid you use in the recipe includes the water you add. Measure the powder and water separately before you mix them. If you save the liquid from more than one tin, keep each label until you’ve checked the ingredients. The contents matter if you use them in a recipe with only a few flavours. For a balanced comparison, choose tins with similar ingredients and check the recipe for whether it uses the liquid directly or asks you to reduce it before whipping.

secciones.h2: How does cooking liquid become a foam?
secciones.texto: The chickpeas give up soluble proteins, starches and fibres to the cooking water. That is what makes the strained liquid useful in a few familiar preparations. Whisking can trap air and form a foam. In mayonnaise, the liquid helps bring the oil and other liquids together. For some batters, it can help the ingredients hold together. Start from the job you want it to do. A meringue recipe gives visible peak cues. The mayonnaise recipe gives a separate blending method. Match the method to the job the egg does in your recipe. If you’re cooking for someone with an ingredient they need to avoid, check the carton or can you opened and check the rest of the recipe separately. A dish can include oils, flavourings or spreads that are unrelated to what is in the chickpea liquid.

secciones.h2: What should you do before using liquid from a tin?
secciones.texto: Look at the label and drain it over a bowl. Check what the recipe needs before you use the liquid. If you are choosing a dessert that calls for foam, read the method for the texture and chilling steps. For a measured amount, weigh the liquid once you’ve drained it.

faq.question: Does chickpea water come from soaking or cooking the beans?

faq.question: Should I check the label on tinned chickpeas?

faq.question: Does the ingredient list tell me how much liquid I’ll get?

intro.title: Vegan mayonnaise with aquafaba at home

intro.h1: How to make vegan mayonnaise with aquafaba at home
intro.texto:
To make aquafaba mayonnaise, blend {mayo_g}g of chilled liquid VERY AQUAFABA with {mustard}g of Dijon mustard, {salt}g of salt and {lemon}g of lemon juice or white wine vinegar. Add {oil}g of oil in a thin stream as you blend. Use a tall jug and a stick blender, then refrigerate the finished mayonnaise.

If you’re making mayo for sandwiches or a bowl of potato salad, a tall jug gives you room to blend without the mixture spreading across a wide bowl.

intro.title: When aquafaba works as a plant-based egg substitute

intro.h1: When to use aquafaba as a plant-based egg substitute
intro.texto:
Aquafaba is a plant-based egg substitute made from chickpea cooking liquid. It can whip into foam for meringues, help hold suitable batters together and combine oil and liquid in mayonnaise. Use a recipe tested with aquafaba when the eggs do more than one job, such as giving a sponge both lift and structure.

Before you change your favourite recipe, read the mixing steps. An egg stirred into pancake batter has a different job from whites whipped in a separate bowl.

secciones.h2: What else should you check?
secciones.texto: Aquafaba can help with the job the egg does, but the finished dish also depends on its other ingredients. Look at milk, butter, fillings and decorations if you’re cooking vegan. If the recipe needs something the egg gives beyond binding or foam, start with a recipe designed for the result you want.

If the instructions tell you to whip whites until they hold their shape, choose a recipe that gives aquafaba its own whipping and folding instructions. If the egg goes into batter as a liquid, see whether the mixture depends mainly on binding. A familiar pancake or muffin can be a place to try a small swap.

For a sauce that needs the oil and other liquids to stay together, follow a measured aquafaba mayonnaise recipe. The amount of oil and how slowly you pour it are part of that method.

secciones.h2: Separate the substitution from the finished dish
secciones.texto:
A recipe can use eggs in more than one place. Read the ingredient list for a wash, filling, topping or separate yolks as well as the batter. You may be able to use aquafaba to coat a pastry even when the filling calls for a different substitute. If you are cooking vegan, check the dairy and other ingredients separately.

Choose a tested method or make a small trial when the egg provides more than one function. A génoise that gets its lift from whipped whole eggs is a different decision from a batter where you mix the egg in with the other liquids.

secciones.h2: Move to a quantity once the method fits
secciones.texto: Use the amount in a recipe written for aquafaba. If you are adapting an egg-based recipe, use the stated conversion as a starting measure and see how the first test cooks. Use the listed weight when your recipe already calls for aquafaba. If you are changing several ingredients at once, start with a recipe that already uses those ingredients. Take notes once you know the result is worth repeating.

faq.question: What is the difference between binding and whipping?

secciones.h2: If you have a stick blender, try mayonnaise

secciones.h2: If you have a mixer, try meringues

If you’re deciding what to do with a quantity you’ve already drained, pick a recipe based on the amount you have. Please drink responsibly.

secciones.h2: Where can you check the formats you can order?
secciones.texto: Use the buying options for your country and confirm what the seller lists. If you want a second use for the aquafaba, start with the easy aquafaba recipes you can make with the equipment you already have.

secciones.h2: Choose a pack from your actual plans for the week
secciones.texto:
Write down what the mayo is for before you decide how much aquafaba to buy. A batch for sandwiches or potato salad needs {mayo_g}g of chilled liquid. That amount is a useful starting point for shopping. The rest of the aquafaba is only useful to you if you have another recipe for it or can store it for later.

If you already plan to make a dessert, check its liquid dose as well. Put the amount for every recipe on one list. For a single batch of mayo, powder gives you a way to prepare only what you need.

secciones.h2: Use the recipe to make sense of the pack size
secciones.texto: Read the ingredient list before buying. For this recipe, the oil, mustard and lemon juice or vinegar also matter because the method combines them while you blend. A tall jug and a stick blender help you work with the measured amounts. Check you have the equipment as well as enough aquafaba. If you shop for powder, weigh the recipe’s dose after preparing it. If you shop for liquid, pour the dose into a separate container and return the opened carton to the fridge. Freeze any portion you won’t use within {opened_days} days of opening.

secciones.h2: Think about what you’ll make next
secciones.texto: Pick something you already like rather than buying a larger pack for a recipe you might never make. If you decide to use the rest for a dessert, the beginner aquafaba guide can help you decide between a bowl of mousse and a tray of meringues based on the equipment you have.

faq.question: How much liquid aquafaba goes into mayo?
faq.answer: The recipe uses {mayo_g}g of chilled liquid for one batch.

faq.question: Should I choose a carton if mayo is all I make?
faq.answer: A carton makes sense if you will use the rest within {opened_days} days of opening. With powder you can prepare only what you need.

faq.question: Should I add powder straight to the oil?
faq.answer: Prepare the aquafaba with water first and weigh the recipe’s amount before you blend.

faq.question: Is the storage advice for the carton also for the finished mayo?
faq.answer: The carton’s instructions apply to opened aquafaba. Keep finished mayonnaise refrigerated and follow the mayonnaise recipe’s handling guidance.

faq.question: Should I buy based on how many jars a pack could make?
faq.answer: Start with how many batches you actually plan to blend. Then account for any other recipes that will use the same aquafaba.
